NVDA.rationale: NVIDIA exhibits exceptional fundamental health with explosive revenue growth (Q3 FY2026 revenue of $57.01B, +22% QoQ), industry-leading margins (gross margin ~70%, operating margin ~58%, net margin ~52%), and a fortress balance sheet (debt-to-equity of 0.085, $118.9B equity). The company dominates AI infrastructure with ~80-92% GPU market share and a deep software moat via CUDA. However, the stock trades at a P/E of 56.6x and P/B of 48.9x, which are at the upper end of its 12-month range (P/E 43.2-63.5), suggesting the market has already priced in substantial growth. The near-term catalyst is the May 20 Q1 FY2027 earnings report with $78B revenue guidance, but historical patterns show NVDA often declines post-earnings. Risks include increasing competition from custom ASICs (Broadcom, Google TPU, AWS Trainium), export control headwinds, and a class-action lawsuit. The forward P/E of ~22-24x cited in some articles suggests the stock is reasonably valued relative to its growth trajectory, but the trailing multiple is elevated. Net: excellent business quality and trajectory, but valuation is fair-to-slightly-rich versus its own history, limiting upside to a mild positive score.
